claims.title: The second candidate's 62.5% cannot be rewritten as a daily quota
claims.conclusion: The daily author-quota interpretations in X Algorithm Playbook and SocialPilot extend the scope: 0.625 corresponds to an author's second-ranked candidate within one candidate pool; it does not imply the second post of a day, a maximum of three, or a gap of at least four hours.
conditions: Using the author-diversity multiplier to explain 62.5%
Multiple candidates from the same author enter the same scoring operation
claims.practical_meaning: Schedule according to whether content adds a new problem, evidence, or progress; distinguish competition within one batch from daily limits.

check.when: When a draft mentions downranking the second post, three posts daily, or recovery after four hours
verify: Replace daily publication order with score order within the current candidate pool
Check for a separate time counter; this function has none
check.if_missing: If no independent timing rule can be supplied, remove the algorithmic guarantee of a fixed waiting period.

limits: Competition within the same batch may still exist
Correcting the daily-limit misreading does not mean rapid posting has no effect whatsoever

claims.title: The author-diversity formula decays by score order within one batch
claims.conclusion: The author multiplier is (1−floor)×decay_factor^k＋floor; VM Ranker's public defaults are decay=0.5 and floor=0.25, giving m(k)=0.75×0.5^k＋0.25. Starting at 0, k follows score order among the same author's candidates in the current pool; the sequence is 1, 0.625, 0.4375 and approaches 0.25.
conditions: Same-author candidates within a single batch call
Publication order is not k; a later high-scoring post can also have k=0
claims.practical_meaning: Explain competition within a batch using the current candidate order; prioritize independent content value when scheduling and choosing topics.

check.when: When a draft contains the author-decay formula, 62.5%, or calculations based on publication order
needed: Author IDs and original scores of candidates in the same batch
verify: Order by score rather than time
Explain that the sequence approaches a floor rather than zero
check.if_missing: Without the candidate pool and actual parameters, illustrate only the public defaults; do not assign a multiplier to a specific post.

limits: This affects ranking scores, not exposure directly
Public defaults do not guarantee identical values for every request
